verdicts.rationale: Comparing bedroughness_init with bedroughness_update confirms that the latter omits mincf and gives the grain-size U branch a different upper bound. The final maximum of 1 does not restore mincf or make the directional bounds equivalent.

The dynamic-roughness branches divide by dstem or droot, including the non-eroded branch when droot is zero. params.F90 accepts zero for both length scales, and neither the vegetation mask nor initialization supplies a positive substitute.

The coefficient-file read and the update formulas provide no nonzero/logarithm-domain validation for Chezy or White-Colebrook inputs. Scalar readkey bounds are warnings unless strict is requested, and a clamp after the division or logarithm cannot prevent its invalid evaluation.

The ventilation formula divides by cfu before its blphi regularization, and subsequently also evaluates 1/cfu. Wetu tests depth rather than friction, while zero friction can enter through the coefficient input, so the wet mask does not neutralize the singularity.

For zero infiltration, the nonnegative branch replaces zero blphi by -1e-4, giving a factor greater than one rather than its exact limit of one. With nonzero flow and ordinary cfu below one, the subsequent cap and multiplication retain the small spurious shear increment.

verdicts.rationale: solver_free deallocates residual and work without clearing initialized, while solver_solvemat relies on that flag to initialize them. Although the internal driver does not call solver_free, the public free-then-solve sequence described by the claim really bypasses allocation.

The saved dimensions and solver settings can become incompatible only on reuse with changed grid/configuration or an external parameter change. They remain consistent throughout an ordinary fixed-configuration run, but neither solver_solvemat nor solver_free implements the required reinitialization for that later lifecycle.

The normal nonhydrostatic caller omits fixshallow, so zero or near-zero elimination pivots remain unchecked for degenerate or poorly conditioned matrices; the wet-cell identity rows do not constrain all active slope-dependent rows. Groundwater callers explicitly enabling fixshallow do have a tiny-pivot replacement, so this is not a universal failure of every Thomas call.

neutralizer.quote:
if (present(fixshallow)) then
         lfixshallow = fixshallow
      else
         lfixshallow = .false.
      endif

      fac    = amat(1,1,jindex)
      if (abs(fac)<tiny(0.d0) .and. lfixshallow) then
         fac = sign(tiny(0.d0),fac)
      endif
      x(1,jindex) = rhs(1,jindex)/fac

      !forward elimination
      do i=2,nx+1
         cmat(i)  = amat(3,i-1,jindex)/fac
         fac      = amat(1,i,jindex)-amat(2,i,jindex)*cmat(i)
         if (abs(fac)<tiny(0.d0) .and. lfixshallow) then
            fac = sign(tiny(0.d0),fac)
         endif
         x(i,jindex) = (rhs(i,jindex)-amat(2,i,jindex)*x(i-1,jindex))/fac

The standard driver starts at t=0 and advances the clock before the first vegetation update, which normally makes t equal dt and initializes totT.
